Download the build for your computer.

**Windows** — `PiTrac-Easy-Connect-windows.zip`. Extract the dedicated
`PiTrac Easy-Connect` folder as a unit. Do not copy the executable out of that
folder. Windows may warn that it does not recognise the program; choose
**More info**, then **Run anyway**.

**macOS** — use `PiTrac-Easy-Connect-macos-apple-silicon.zip` for an M1 or
later Mac, or `PiTrac-Easy-Connect-macos-intel.zip` for a real Intel Mac.
Extract and move the complete `.app`, then right-click it and choose **Open**
the first time.

**Linux x86-64** — install WebKitGTK 4.1, extract the dedicated
`PiTrac Easy-Connect` directory, and run the executable inside it. Keep the
directory together.

### v0.4.6

- Establishes the safe desktop updater foundation: verified package manifests,
  an independent updater helper, journaled same-filesystem promotion, exact
  restart acknowledgement, and automatic rollback before the prior version is
  removed.
- Refuses automatic replacement when Windows or Linux is run as a loose
  executable from Downloads, Desktop, Documents, a home directory, a drive or
  filesystem root, or any directory that does not satisfy the dedicated
  installation contract.
- Preserves valid macOS application-bundle symlinks while rejecting archive
  traversal, escaping links, duplicate paths, and special files.
- Keeps status checks asynchronous, exposes download progress and cancellation,
  and persists the exact desktop/Pi release target across restart or loss of
  network access.
- Removes new-window and external-browser requests from all shipped desktop and
  portal sources.

v0.4.5 does not contain this updater. Existing v0.4.5 users must install v0.4.6
manually. The first normal automatic update based on this foundation will be
v0.4.6 to v0.4.7.

`PiTrac-Easy-Connect-<version>.pyz` is the verified Raspberry Pi service-update
payload used by Easy-Connect. It is not a Linux desktop application.

### Checking what you downloaded

Every release file is covered by GitHub build provenance and `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
For example:

```
gh attestation verify PiTrac-Easy-Connect-windows.zip --repo TylerPardun/pitrac-easy-connect
```

This provenance is not a paid Windows or Apple code-signing certificate, so
the first-launch platform warnings described above still apply.
